title: Steering Column — The Mechanical Steering Path
introduction:
I use this exploded drawing to follow the handoff of rotation from the steering wheel toward the steering gear. The separated assemblies make the connections easier to see; their spacing on the page is illustrative, not their installed spacing.

Match the drawing’s callouts to the adjacent table, then follow the column, shaft sections and coupling along that path. This is a component overview. Disconnection, the required collapsed check and refitting need their separate service instructions.

edits.text: Read the drawing as a connected mechanical path carrying steering-wheel rotation toward the steering gear.
How the Steering Column Connects to the Gear

The steering column forms the mechanical link between the steering wheel and the steering gear. The wheel mounts to a shaft passing through the column’s center, where bearings keep the shaft centered. The upper and lower steering column shafts continue the connection from the column to the gear. The lower steering column shaft is collapsible and must be measured whenever it has been disconnected from either the upper shaft or the coupling.
edits.why: The bearings support the rotating shaft inside the column, while the connected shaft sections carry that rotation onward. The collapsible lower shaft has a required measurement after either specified disconnection; appearance alone does not satisfy that requirement. For work involving disconnection, use the separate [Steering Column Collapsed Check](#/document/G1721912) for the measurement method and acceptance criteria. This overview does not teach that check.
